subject: Literature
subcategory: Classic Novels That Changed the World
title: War and Peace and the Epic Tradition
description: A 60-second lesson on War and Peace and the Epic Tradition.

hook.text: Leo Tolstoy spent six years writing a novel so large that he declared it was not actually a novel at all.

buildup.text: War and Peace wove together five aristocratic families, Napoleon's invasion, and the meaning of history.

discovery.text: At over half a million words, it remains one of the longest and most ambitious novels ever completed.

twist.text: Tolstoy argued that great leaders do not shape history; history sweeps leaders along like everyone else.

climax.text: War and Peace redefined what a novel could be: not just a story, but an entire philosophy of civilization.

punchline.text: One book tried to contain all of human existence.

quiz.question: What was Tolstoy's view of history in War and Peace?
options: Great leaders single-handedly shape all events
History sweeps leaders along like everyone else
History is completely random with no patterns
